title: Policy-driven request routing & priority simulator for enterprise data-control requests
creator: Morgan Lee
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit heterogeneous data-control requests (log redaction, retention changes, PII export, audit dumps). Triage is manual, inconsistent across regions, and slow for high-risk legal requests. We need a reproducible, policy-driven routing engine plus a lightweight priority simulator so PMs, CSMs, and Legal can predict SLA and escalation outcomes before approving implementation scope.

Scope: Build a policy template library and routing ruleset capable of classifying incoming requests into policy-buckets (Legal-High, Security-High, Compliance-Regional, Ops-Low-cost), compute a priority score, and emit a recommended routing target (Console self-serve, Solutions Eng, Legal review, SRE-runbook). Deliver a web-based simulator (internal) that lets operators paste request metadata and see the score, route, and estimated SLO. Integrate results with the existing governance intake dashboard and create canned responses/templates for each route.

Out of scope: Full automation of redaction execution, on-prem export mechanics, and customer-visible SLA pages (these will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Policy template library with at least 6 templates covering common request types: log redaction (PII regex), retention increase/decrease, audit export (full/partial), PII export, anonymization request, and deletion request
Routing ruleset engine that returns route + priority score for synthetic test cases with >= 95% agreement against SMEs' manual labels (sample set of 120 requests)
Internal simulator UI that accepts request metadata, shows score breakdown, selected policy template, recommended route, estimated resolution SLO, and manual override
Integration: each simulated decision can produce a pre-populated intake ticket (Linear) or an email draft to trigger Solutions/Legal workflows
Operator docs and playbook (Confluence) with decision rationale, escalation matrix, and response templates
decision_rubric: Weights (default): legal_risk=40, customer_sla_importance=25, operational_cost=20, cross_region_impact=10, anomaly_flag=5
Legal risk indicators: presence of regulatory jurisdiction tag (EU/UK/CA), request type (PII export or deletion), and customer contract clause references
Customer SLA importance: paying tier, active incident, and contractual SLAs; increases priority by 1.5x if "SLA-critical" flagged
Operational cost: measured as estimated engineering hours (bands: <4h, 4-16h, >16h), larger costs reduce priority unless customer-impacted
Anomaly flag: requests with unknown patterns or free-text that match heuristic confidence < 0.6 escalate to human review
routing_matrix: Legal-High (score >= 70 && legal_risk >= 30) => route: Legal review -> Solutions Eng intake -> SLA: 7 business days
Compliance-Regional (cross_region_impact >= 20 && request_type in [retention, export]) => route: Compliance ops -> Regional PM -> SLA: 10 business days
Ops-Low-cost (score < 40 && estimated_eng_hours < 4) => route: Self-serve guidance + template -> SLA: 3 business days
Security-High (anomaly_flag == true || pii_payload_detected==true) => route: Security triage -> SRE/IR -> immediate 48-hour acknowledgement
implementation_notes: Classification model: start with deterministic rules + regex for PII detection, add lightweight ML classifier (logistic reg) if deterministic coverage < 85%
Rules engine: implement as a small serverless service that evaluates policy templates and outputs score vector; embed versioning to support rollouts
Simulator UI: internal-only React app behind SSO; copy of route logic mirrored client-side for instant feedback with server-side validation
Audit trail: every simulated decision must generate a decision artifact (JSON) logged to governance audit S3 and visible in the Console intake history
Canary: release rules engine in two phases: dry-run (evaluate and log but do not change routing) for 2 weeks, then opt-in routing for CSM-managed customers
